summary.intent: Execute Phase 34 (E2E Test Expansion & Staging Baselines) — create account cleanup helpers, media/streaming test suites, batch download tests, and capture staging performance baselines.
summary.outcome: All 4 plans executed and verified (13/13 must-haves passed). Real 200-client sustained load baselines captured after diagnosing that simultaneous test runs (not a bypass bug) caused the initial failures.

repo: Staging Web3Auth init takes ~22.7s; wallet button timeout in journey-timing.spec.ts was 20s and needed increasing to 45s for staging runs.
playwright.config.ts did not respect BASE_URL env var for targeting staging — needed explicit process.env.BASE_URL override and conditional webServer startup suppression.
cleanup-helpers.ts deleteAccountViaPage was hardcoded to localhost:3000; needed to derive API URL dynamically from the page URL to work on staging.
tests/load vitest.config.ts had no dotenv loading — .env file was silently ignored; fixed by sourcing .env in shell before running vitest.

Staging throttle bypass (X-Throttle-Bypass-Secret header) works correctly end-to-end. Initial 429 failures were caused by running two load tests simultaneously against the same staging instance, not a bypass bug.
CI load tests pass because NODE_ENV=test sets throttle limits to 200/sec; staging uses production limits (10/sec) so the bypass header is critical for load testing.
BYO load test harness (tests/load/src/scenarios/byo-capacity-ceiling.test.ts) steps through 50→100→200→500→1000 clients to find Pinata contention ceiling.
createClientPool(200) succeeds in ~38.7s with bypass header — no rate limiting at that concurrency when run solo.

code.finding: waitFor timeout was 20_000ms — too short for staging Web3Auth init; increased to 45_000ms
Added process.env.BASE_URL override for baseURL and conditional webServer block suppression when targeting staging
deleteAccountViaPage was hardcoded to localhost API; fixed to derive API URL from page.url() hostname
No dotenv loading — .env file silently ignored by vitest workers; must source .env in shell before running tests

workflow: Cherry-picking between worktree branches into phase branch causes STATE.md merge conflicts every time — needs resolution on each cherry-pick.
Running multiple load tests simultaneously against a shared staging environment saturates it even with throttle bypass — always run load tests sequentially against staging.
GSD worktree cleanup (git worktree remove --force) must be done promptly; stale worktrees cause git.lock file contention in subsequent agents.
The classifyHandoffIfNeeded Claude Code bug causes agents to report 'failed' even when all work completed — always spot-check SUMMARY.md + git commits before treating as failure.
Vitest does not auto-load .env files unlike Jest/create-react-app; must explicitly configure envFile or source env in shell.

friction: 34-04 agent ran in a worktree but commits needed manual cherry-picking to phase branch — no automatic merge.
STATE.md merge conflicts on every cherry-pick from worktree branches slowed Wave 1 merge significantly.
34-03 agent hit a git.lock contention failure on first attempt due to stale 34-04 worktree not being cleaned up in time.
Two load tests running simultaneously caused false throttle failures, leading to a lengthy debugging session that ultimately found no bug.
SSH access to staging VPS timed out, blocking direct Docker env var inspection during diagnosis.
vitest .env loading gap was a red herring that consumed investigation time before the real cause (concurrent tests) was found.
BYO capacity ceiling test ran twice (once colliding, once stale results) before clean solo results were available.
The 200-client sustained load test was killed by the user mid-run; results were captured from partial output.
open_items: New media/streaming test specs (streaming-playback.spec.ts, media-preview.spec.ts) use binary stub fixtures — need a live environment run to confirm they trigger actual AES-CTR/GCM code paths.
BYO capacity ceiling test (50→100→200→500→1000 Pinata clients) never ran cleanly — only had colliding/stale results; needs a solo run.
Sustained load test p95 thresholds are tuned for small client counts and fail at 200 clients even with 0.17% error rate — thresholds need recalibration for the scale.
Caddy reverse proxy rate limiting upstream of NestJS was not investigated as a possible secondary throttle layer.
Faro/Grafana visual inspection for staging traces (Step 3 of 34-04 Task 2) was never completed.
Prometheus metrics check (curl staging /metrics | grep ipfs_operation_duration) was never completed.
The insert-phase 34.1 was created and then reverted — the learnings file at .learnings/2026-03-29-staging-load-test-throttle-bypass.md references this history.
Phase 34 was briefly marked complete in ROADMAP.md/STATE.md then reverted — the roadmap state should be audited to confirm it accurately reflects current status.
